transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I’m here because... well, most days I wake up and it just feels like there's this heavy, gray weight sitting on me. It doesn't really go away. Even when I’m out working with the landscaping crew, or, you know, at home around my kids, I just can’t shake it. It's this low, hollow feeling, like I’m just... going through the motions of everything.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been... about three years and three months now. Yeah. It started right around the time the groundskeeping contract changed at work. They switched up our schedule, and those longer days just kind of took over my life. It's been pretty much like this ever since.
Since this began, has there been a period of two months or longer when you did not feel depressed or empty?
No... no, I haven't. Honestly, I don't think there's been a time where it lifted for even a couple of weeks, let alone two whole months. It's just... it's just always there, every single day.
During this time, have you lost interest in or pleasure from activities you usually enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I normally do. I still watch the games on Sunday, and I still like hanging out with my kids. I haven't really lost interest in any of that stuff... it's just that the heavy feeling is always there while I'm doing it.
During this period, have you often felt tired or low in energy?

Yeah, I'm tired all the time. By midmorning, my body feels like I’ve already put in a full day of work. And it doesn't really matter if I rest... even after sleeping in on a Sunday, I still just drag through simple things. Stuff like loading up the tools, checking over the job plans, or just making dinner at night... it all just takes so much effort.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions during this period?

No, not really. I mean, my head feels pretty clear most of the time. I know what needs to get done on the job sites, and I can still figure out the schedules and order the supplies without messing it up. So, no, my concentration seems fine. It's just the energy to actually do it that's missing.
During this period, have you often felt hopeless about the future?

Yeah, honestly, I do. I just keep telling myself that this is just how my life is now. It feels like no matter how hard I work, or how much I try to get back to doing my own garden or going to those music nights... nothing is really going to turn around. It's just going to stay like this.
